result.summary:
All 6 ACs met. Implemented per the design doc's sections with two deliberate, disclosed deviations from what the design guessed (both resolved against real source, not silently assumed):

1. OQ-2 (sub-process child lookup): confirmed no by-parent-instance-id context function exists on Letflow.Instances/Letflow.Engine. Resolved via a direct, test-local Repo query against InstanceProjection.parent_instance_id (a real, populated column -- Letflow.Engine.SubProcess.insert_child_instance_projection/8 sets it on every sub-process child row) -- the narrowest read consistent with 'no context function exists yet.'

2. OQ-3 (terminal END node identity): RE-RESOLVED DIFFERENTLY than either candidate the design named. Read lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:373-379 (dispatch_end/3): a token is unconditionally dropped from instance_state.tokens the instant it reaches an END node. This means InstanceProjection.current_nodes -- the design's own first-named candidate -- is ALWAYS [] once status == :completed, for every terminal END node alike; it cannot distinguish end-false-positive from end-closed. Confirmed empirically this session (both scenarios' current_nodes were [] after completion, not [terminal_node_id] as guessed). The real, queryable distinguishing signal turned out to be each scenario's own last relevant TASK_COMPLETED/SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED event payload's 'activated_nodes' field (via Letflow.Instances.history/3) -- for the false-positive scenario, severity-classification's own completion event shows activated_nodes == [] (direct route to end-false-positive); for the critical scenario, the SAME completion event shows activated_nodes == ['corrective-action-subprocess'] (non-terminal at that point), and the LATER SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED event on the parent's own stream shows activated_nodes == [] once corrective-action-subprocess completes into end-closed. This is disclosed in the test module's own moduledoc and in both scenario YAMLs' comments, not silently substituted.

Also found and worked around a real, pre-existing Engine defect (REQ-062, out of this requirement's scope to fix, flagged not silently patched): a SUB_PROCESS child that completes SYNCHRONOUSLY within the same hop-chain transaction that spawned it causes two Ecto.Multi steps to collide on the same {:task_records, parent_instance_id} key (lib/letflow/engine.ex's append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/5 chaining into Letflow.Engine.SubProcess.append_start_multi/7's own maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6 branch) -- raises 'cannot merge Multi' (Ecto.Multi.merge_results/3). Worked around test-locally, same class of workaround REQ-206 already used for the SERVICE_TASK gap: @simple_child_graph (the corrective-action-subprocess node's child definition) is START -> HUMAN_TASK -> END, not a synchronously-completing START -> END, so the child's own completion is driven independently (its own Letflow.Engine.complete_task/3 call, own transaction) rather than cascading inside the parent's hop-chain transaction. Documented in the test module with a full explanation; this is a real Engine gap someone should file a follow-up issue for, not this requirement's own defect.

Files delivered: 4 scenario YAMLs under test/fixtures/simulation/vortex/scenarios/ (production-order-above-threshold, supplier-quality-deviation-critical, supplier-quality-deviation-false-positive, entity-list-filter-and-page -- the last structurally complete but never loaded/run per §4.3). test/support/simulation/runner.ex extended with :audit_event_ordering (Scenario.expected_outcome().verification.method's 4th value, a new verify_outcome/2 clause, and a shared find_audit_entry/2 helper factored out of the existing :audit_event clause -- no behavior change to the 3 existing methods). test/support/simulation/scenario_fixture.ex's @method_atoms extended with 'audit_event_ordering' => :audit_event_ordering. test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs: 4 describe blocks mirroring req206_swiftroute_test.exs's structure (DataCase async: false, Sandbox :auto, TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug('req207'), teardown dropping the tenant schema), @simple_production_order_graph and @simple_supplier_deviation_graph as inline module attributes (not committed process_*.yaml files, matching REQ-206's @simple_approval_graph precedent). test/reports/req207-vortex-scenario-findings.yaml populated with real observed values from this session's own mix test run (real timestamps, real activated_nodes evidence, real disposition counts) -- no placeholders.

Gates: mix compile --warnings-as-errors -- clean, 0 warnings. mix format --check-formatted -- clean after one auto-format pass on the test file (list literals). Self-review: no tenant/user input string-interpolated into raw SQL (the one ~s(...) DROP SCHEMA interpolation is test-local schema_name from TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1, matching req206_swiftroute_test.exs's own established pattern verbatim, not new risk); no unresolved {:ok, _} = match on an external-I/O-reachable path (every new match in runner.ex is inside a with/case that routes failure to :fail with observed evidence, matching the existing 3 methods' discipline); no new public functions added (all new runner.ex/scenario_fixture.ex functions are private, no @doc gap). mix test test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs run against real Postgres (Docker letflow-2-postgres-1, port 5472, started this session -- was down at session start): 'Finished in 7.1 seconds (0.00s async, 7.1s sync)' / 'Result: 4 passed', 0 failures, real quoted output. Did not touch lib/letflow/process_instance.ex or README.md's state diagram (out of scope -- no state-machine shape changed). Concurrent-session check: git fetch + git log before AND immediately before push both showed origin/feature/WF02-REQ207-20260901 unchanged at 0888cfc8 (this run's own starting point) -- no sibling Step 2a work found; push was a clean fast-forward (0888cfc8..f899274e).

issues.title: Pre-existing Engine defect (REQ-062): a synchronously-completing SUB_PROCESS child collides its own Ecto.Multi :task_records step against the parent hop-chain's own step for the same instance_id
issues.detail: lib/letflow/engine.ex's append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/5 (called from build_complete_task_tail_multi/6, the complete_task/3 hop-chain tail) appends SubProcess.append_start_multi/7 onto the SAME Multi that already appended build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3 for the parent's own instance_id. When the spawned child completes SYNCHRONOUSLY (its own advance_until_stable/4 reaches :completed inside prepare_child_activation/4, before any Multi step exists), append_start_multi/7's maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6 branch chains append_completion_multi/5 -> build_completion_write_steps/12 -> TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records(parent_instance_id, ...) (keyed {:task_records, parent_instance_id}) into the SAME transaction -- colliding with the parent hop-chain's own earlier {:task_records, parent_instance_id} step (via build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3). Raises RuntimeError 'cannot merge Multi; the following operations were found in both Ecto.Multi: [task_records: "<parent_instance_id>"]' (Ecto.Multi.merge_results/3), surfaced to the caller as Plug.Conn.WrapperError. Reproduced directly this session against a real running instance via POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/complete when the completing task's hop chain enters a SUB_PROCESS node whose child definition is a synchronously-completing START->END graph. Worked around test-locally (this requirement's own child definition uses a pending HUMAN_TASK instead, completed independently), but the underlying Engine code path is unfixed. Recommend filing a follow-up issue against REQ-062's own module (lib/letflow/engine.ex / lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex) at Step Final.
